title: Climbing Mount Olympus: Full Guide
excerpt: Mytikas, 2,918 m, is the highest summit in Greece. The full guide: the route from Gortsias to Prionia, the huts, the final scramble, difficulty, season and cost.
seoTitle: Climbing Mount Olympus to Mytikas: Route, Huts, Season and Cost

content.value: On the third morning of the trip, the group leaves Petrostrouga Hut, at 1,940 m, for the longest day of the trek: the climb across the Muses Plateau to Mytikas, 2,918 m (9,573 ft), the highest summit of Mount Olympus and of all Greece. Climbing Olympus is a 6-day journey from Thessaloniki and back, with three days on the mountain, two nights in mountain huts and a summit day of 6 to 8 hours. No previous climbing experience is required, but the final section to the summit runs through a narrow couloir where you climb using your hands, so you need good fitness, proper mountain boots and respect for the weather. Our trekking season runs from June to October.

For many trekkers, Olympus is their first multi-day mountain journey abroad: a mountain wrapped in mythology, pine forests, nights in huts and a genuine rocky summit. This guide puts everything you need to know in order: what the mountain is, how our route works day by day, what awaits on the final section to Mytikas and what gear is used there, how hard it is, when to go, how to get there and what the price includes.
The mountain of the gods

Mount Olympus rises in northern Greece, between Macedonia and Thessaly, a short distance from the shores of the Aegean Sea. It is the highest mountain in the country, and in Greek mythology it is the home of the Olympian gods. The mountain is protected as a national park, and its slopes climb from the coastal area to bare rocky summits, so within a single day of walking you pass from dense pine forests to open high plateaus, with views that reach the sea on a clear day.

Olympus is not a single peak but a massif of several summits, and the highest of them is Mytikas, 2,918 m. Our route leads to the main summits of the mountain, Skala and Mytikas, and when the weather allows, the group stands on Mytikas itself.

The base for the trip is Litochoro, a small town at the foot of the mountain, about an hour and a half by road from Thessaloniki airport. From there a transfer takes you to the start of the trail, and you return there at the end of the descent, to a hot shower and a hotel bed.

The weather on Olympus changes quickly: clouds, wind and lightning can appear without warning, even on a day that began clear. In summer, clouds tend to build around the summits in the afternoon, which is why summit day starts early. All decisions on the trail are made by the guides.
Our route, day by day

The HighAir Olympus trek lasts 6 days, from landing in Thessaloniki to the flight home. It climbs from Gortsias, crosses the upper mountain via the Muses Plateau and Mytikas, and descends to Prionia. This is the itinerary:

items: Day 1: arrival in Thessaloniki and a transfer of about an hour and a half to the hotel in Litochoro. Check-in and a briefing with the guiding team ahead of the climb.
Day 2: transfer to Gortsias, the starting point at 1,140 m, and a walk on a marked trail through dense forest and rocky ground to Petrostrouga Hut (1,940 m). 7 km, 3 to 4 hours, 800 m of ascent.
Day 3: from Petrostrouga Hut via the Muses Plateau to the summit of Mytikas (2,918 m), weather permitting, and descent to Kakkalos Hut. 15 km, 6 to 8 hours, 978 m of ascent and 268 m of descent.
Day 4: descent from Kakkalos Hut to Prionia (1,140 m), through forests and viewpoints, and a transfer back to the hotel in Litochoro. 8 km, 4 to 5 hours, 1,510 m of descent.
Day 5: a canyoning day on the Orlias River, about 4 hours, and back to Litochoro.
Day 6: breakfast, transfer to Thessaloniki airport and the flight home.

content.value: Accommodation changes with the route. Three nights are spent in a 3-star hotel in Litochoro on a bed and breakfast basis: the first night, and the nights after the descent from the mountain and after the canyoning day. On the mountain you sleep two nights in mountain huts, in shared rooms: at Petrostrouga Hut, at 1,940 m, and at Kakkalos Hut on the Muses Plateau, at about 2,650 m. Meals can be bought at the hut cafeteria from the menu, and they are not included in the price.

content.value: The final section to Mytikas

Summit day starts early at Petrostrouga Hut. A winding trail climbs from the hut to the Muses Plateau, a broad high plateau below the main summits, and from there you continue to Mytikas. The last part is not a walking trail: it runs through a narrow couloir, about a kilometer of scrambling in which you hold on to the rock with your hands, and on some sections you feel the drop beneath your feet very clearly. It is not technical rock climbing, but it is the section that sets Olympus apart from an ordinary trek, and it demands concentration, sure footing and full attention to the instructions of the guides.

The gullies and rock slopes of Olympus hold loose stones, and a stone dislodged by one climber can fall on whoever is climbing below. That is why it is common practice to wear a helmet on the upper section toward Mytikas. Climbing equipment, a harness and a helmet, is included in the price of our trek.

content.alt: Climbers sitting on a steep rock slope inside a gully, one in a blue helmet, with a rope running along the rock and forested valleys and ridges in haze below
content.caption: Climbers in a steep rocky gully above forested valleys

content.value: Footwear matters more here than anywhere else on the route. You need hiking or mountain boots with ankle support and a grippy sole, and trail running shoes are not suitable for the Mytikas scramble.

content.title: ✦ Weather first
content.value: The climb to Mytikas goes ahead only when the weather allows. If clouds, strong wind or lightning approach, the guides decide how to continue, and the route may change. In the mountains there is no promise of a summit, only a commitment to safety.

From the summit you descend with the same care you climbed, to Kakkalos Hut on the Muses Plateau, for the second night on the mountain. Many incidents in the mountains happen on the way down, when legs are tired and concentration drops, so the descent from the rocky section is slow and controlled. The next day the long descent continues, through the forests, to Prionia.
How hard is climbing Olympus

We grade the trek as moderate, and no previous climbing experience is required. If you can walk about 20 km a day, enjoy a challenge and are highly motivated, the trek can suit you. The real difficulty is three consecutive days of effort: 800 m of ascent on the second day, a summit day of 15 km and 6 to 8 hours, and the following day a descent of 1,510 m that works mainly the knees. Trekking poles help a great deal on that descent.

Altitude is part of the picture too, though on a modest scale. At 2,918 m most people need no special acclimatization days, but some feel a mild headache, fatigue or shortness of breath with effort. The itinerary raises the sleeping altitude gradually: the first night on the mountain is at 1,940 m, and the second, after the summit, at about 2,650 m. Anyone who feels the symptoms getting worse should tell the guides straight away.

The best preparation is long hikes with a pack in the months before departure, with plenty of climbs and just as many descents. Before the trek you receive a personal gear checklist and an online gear consultation, and the group meets the guide on an online preparation call. Every participant must provide a medical certificate and a health declaration as a condition for departure, and anyone who does not meet the health or physical requirements cannot join.
When to climb Olympus

Our Olympus trekking season runs from June to October. In these months the huts are open, and the snow has usually melted from most of the route. Early in the season, and in years after a snowy winter, patches of snow may remain on the upper mountain, and then the guides decide whether and how to cross them.

In July and August it is hot in the valleys, and the chance of afternoon thunderstorms rises. As fall advances the heat eases, but nights at altitude grow colder, so bring warm layers for the huts. In any season the weather on the mountain can change within a short time, which is why summit day starts early.
A day on the water: canyoning on the Orlias River

After the descent from the mountain comes a different kind of day. On day 5 a short transfer takes you from Litochoro to the Orlias River for about 4 hours of canyoning: rappelling down waterfalls, swimming in natural pools and scrambling over rocks, accompanied by professional guides. It is a day of water, lush vegetation and views of Olympus from below, and it is included in the price of the trek.

content.alt: A group in wetsuits and helmets standing in a green pool below a waterfall, cheering for the camera, while one person descends the waterfall on a rope
content.caption: A natural pool below a waterfall on the canyoning day

content.value: Basic swimming ability is required on the canyoning day, and anyone who does not swim should let us know in advance. After the activity you return to Litochoro for the last night before the flight.
Getting there and entering Greece

The trip starts and ends in Thessaloniki. International flights are not included in the price. Transfers from the airport to the hotel in Litochoro and back are included, and the drive takes about an hour and a half.

Greece is part of the Schengen Area. EU citizens travel with a valid passport or national ID card. UK, US, Canadian and Australian citizens enter without a visa, with a valid passport, for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. On a first entry to the Schengen Area, non-EU travelers are registered in the European Union's digital Entry/Exit System (EES): you give fingerprints and have your photograph taken at the border, so allow extra time at passport control. ETIAS, the online travel authorization the EU plans to require from visa-exempt travelers, is not yet in operation (as of 2026). Check the validity of your passport and the current entry rules before you fly.
Travel and medical insurance is not included in the price. Before you buy, make sure the policy covers mountain hiking and climbing up to 2,918 m, including rescue, as well as the canyoning day.
Who it suits

Olympus especially suits those looking for their first multi-day mountain journey abroad: hikers who already walk the trails at home and want to sleep in huts, stand on a genuine summit and be home after six days. It also suits those who have walked in the mountains before and are looking for a short trip with a rocky summit. Anyone uneasy with heights should know that the exposure is felt on the final section to Mytikas, and it is worth talking to us about it before booking.

Good to know: the trek is led by professional local guides who speak English and have long experience leading groups in the mountains. Basic English, enough to follow instructions on the trail, is worth having. Following the instructions of the crew is mandatory, and the route may change according to the weather and the judgment of the guides.

And anyone who feels after Olympus that they want to go higher can continue to Kilimanjaro, 5,895 m, where the main challenge is altitude and acclimatization. We have written a full guide to that mountain.
Olympus with HighAir

Our Olympus trek lasts 6 days, departs in the season between June and October, and is limited to 10 participants. The price is 1,750 euros per person, and the success rate we publish on the mountain is 98 percent.

The price includes airport transfers from Thessaloniki to the hotel in Litochoro and back, internal transfers to the start of the route and back, 3 nights in a 3-star hotel in Litochoro with breakfast, mountain hut accommodation in shared rooms throughout the climb, professional local English-speaking guides, climbing equipment (harness and helmet), a canyoning day on the Orlias River, all entry permits for the climb, live WhatsApp updates for families during the climb, a personal area in the HighAir app, a detailed gear list and a training plan for the climb, an online gear consultation, an online preparation call with your group and guide before departure, support with flight and travel insurance questions before departure, a gift kit with a cap and a dry-fit shirt, and a meaningful donation to the fight against cancer.

Not included: international flights, travel and medical insurance with evacuation cover (required), lunch and dinner at the hotel in Litochoro, meals in the huts (paid locally, from the menu), personal gear (clothing and footwear), tips for the guides (50 euros per person), an extra hotel night if needed, and personal expenses such as drinks, alcohol, laundry, gifts and internet. In the event of an early descent from the mountain, for any reason, the additional costs, such as hotel nights, meals and flight changes, are borne by the trekker.

content.value: A portion of the proceeds from every expedition we run is dedicated to supporting cancer patients, because the mountains, in our view, are also a way of giving back. Everyone who stands on the high summits of the world started once, on one mountain. If Olympus is that mountain for you, we are here.
Frequently asked questions
How many days does it take to climb Olympus?

On the HighAir trek the whole journey lasts 6 days, from landing in Thessaloniki to the flight home. Three of them, days 2 to 4, are on the mountain, with two nights in huts and a summit day of 6 to 8 hours. On day 5 the group goes canyoning on the Orlias River.
Do I need climbing experience to reach Mytikas?

We require no previous climbing experience. If you can walk about 20 km a day and are highly motivated, the trek can suit you. The final section to the summit is about a kilometer of scrambling in a narrow couloir, using your hands, so you need mountain boots with ankle support. Climbing equipment, a harness and a helmet, is included in the price.
When is the season for climbing Olympus?

Our trekking season runs from June to October, when the huts are open and most of the snow has melted. In July and August the chance of afternoon thunderstorms rises, so summit day starts early. The climb to the summit goes ahead only when the weather allows.
Do I need a visa for Greece?

Greece is part of the Schengen Area. EU citizens need only a valid passport or ID card, and UK, US, Canadian and Australian citizens enter without a visa for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, giving fingerprints and a facial photograph at the border on a first entry. Check the current entry rules before you fly, including the start date of ETIAS.
What language do the guides speak?
The trek is led by professional local guides who speak English and have long experience leading groups in the mountains.
